stem.text: Let \( f(x) = - 2 x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 12 x + 3 \). Using the second derivative test where it applies, determine whether f has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at \( x = -2 \) and at \( x = 5 \).

answer_key.label: At \( x = -2 \), f has a relative minimum because \( f'(-2) = 0 \) and \( f''(-2) = 18 > 0 \); at \( x = 5 \), f has no relative extremum because \( f'(5) = -168 \ne 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate: \( f'(x) = - 6 x^{2} - 6 x + 12 \), which factors as \( f'(x) = - 6 \left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right) \).
\( f'(-2) = 0 \), so \( x = -2 \) is a critical point, while \( f'(5) = -168 \ne 0 \), so \( x = 5 \) is not.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points are zeros of the first derivative
second derivative evaluated at the critical point

worked_solution.text: By the second derivative test f has a relative minimum at \( x = -2 \). At \( x = 5 \) the first derivative is not zero, so f has no relative extremum there and the test does not apply.
